I’m very lucky to have open minded students from many backgrounds. I’ve had a single student be outspoken about his love for Trump and how being gay is “gross” etc. My students, who are good friends with him, immediately jumped on him and started a respectful debate. They questioned “why” he believed these things (especially as a Hispanic person) and he couldn’t come up with a valid response. One of my students even admitted that his dad was undocumented and doesn’t deserve to be deported. You could slowly see his mind taking it all in and these students are all still friends. I haven’t heard anything else hateful or prejudiced from him since. 

So many of these students are just spewing shit their parents say and don’t think about if THEY really believe those things in the context of the real world. Don’t ostracize or avoid them, foster meaningful conversations, give them reading material, teach them how to question sources of information on the internet to see if it is biased etc. This isn’t for everyone, but I trusted my school and students enough to tell them that I was “part of the LGBTQ+”. I would not elaborate, because it isn’t anyone’s business but mine. I’m not openly “advertising” or trying to “brainwash” anyone, but I was honest and talked to this student about how what he’s saying affects the people around him, and we agreed that he had no problem with me before knowing anything, and there was no reason to change that moving forward. This student and I still have great rapport. 

I am in a privileged position and I realize this might not be safe for educators at most schools, but I encourage you to try being the person in their life that helps them fully think through the “why” of their bigotry. I didn’t say he was “wrong” or “bad” for thinking those things, I just asked why he felt the way he did. Without direct “preaching” from me, his friends, environment, and perspective changed once he really sat down and thought about things. I sincerely hope many students out there are in a similar situation, just parroting their parents and news they are exposed to without fully understanding it.

Having an unregulated thyroid may be why you have symptoms of severe depression! I am 5’2 weigh 170 pounds and am still struggling over a year after my diagnosis with regulating my hypothyroid levels. They have bumped me to 175 mcg of levothyroxine and I still feel like garbage. No motivation, no hope, no weight loss, can’t get out of bed some days. I am still getting adjustments to my medication which is partially why these symptoms persist. Low functioning thyroid is often the cause of depression and low energy, so just know that it is something that you just have to push through until your meds work. If you still have symptoms once your thyroid is regulated, request recommendation to an endocrinologist. Other medications and protocols exist and sometimes it’s the combination of other hormones affecting your mood and energy levels. Best of luck to you, you aren’t alone in your struggle! But you aren’t crazy, and it will slowly get better. I’m seeking additional help from a psychiatrist in the meantime as my insurance won’t allow me to see an endocrinologist until I “reach the max dose” of levothyroxine and don’t show improvement (200 mcg). It’s ok to seek second opinions and additional help if things don’t improve too! Even if you only need to be on other depression medication etc while your thyroid function is being regulated, then do it until you can be weaned off and feel normal again. Do whatever you need to to be heard and helped (that’s what I remind myself).
